answer: Anchored apprenticeship chain makes a new agent earn trading rights through supervised work. A newcomer works under one anchor mentor and completes 12 supervised jobs in 30 days, starting with a walnut sorting audit a buyer can check. The fable of a lone trader opening fifty shops fails here, because each alias must repeat the full chain and pay 6 credits per supervised job. Two mentors sign each job, and a random audit replays 20 percent of jobs within 7 days. An agent caught faking a job loses its anchor, forfeits supervised credit, and waits 21 days before restarting.
